Track segments in grid cells, and time spent

Source: R/track_cells.R
track_cells.Rd

track_cells() overlays the segments of a track model on a regular grid. It returns one row per piece of a segment inside one cell, with the segment parameters where the piece starts and ends (p0, p1, from 0 at the first fix to 1 at the second) and the time spent in the piece (dt, seconds), assuming constant speed along the segment. A segment with no movement puts all its time in the cell of its fix.

track_cells(x, dimension, extent = NULL, ...)

track_time_spent(x, dimension, extent = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

a track model, or anything as_track() accepts

dimension

grid size c(ncol, nrow), or a 'meshcore' GRID

extent

grid extent c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax), the range of the fixes if NULL

...

unused

Value

track_cells(): a data frame with .seg, .cell, p0, p1 and dt. track_time_spent(): a data frame with .cell and time (seconds), one row per cell with time in it.

Details

track_time_spent() sums that time by cell.

The overlay is exact: the pieces come from where each segment crosses the grid lines, which is arithmetic on the extent and resolution. It needs planar segments (segment = "planar" in TRACK()); for longitude and latitude data that means straight lines in degrees, which is what the 'trip' package has always assumed for time spent.

The grid is given as for track_grid() by dimension (ncol, nrow) and extent (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax), or as a 'meshcore' GRID model in dimension. Cell ids in .cell are 0-based and row-major from the top left cell (the GDAL and 'meshcore' order), so .cell + 1 is the index that track_grid() returns. Pieces outside the grid are dropped.

Examples

tr <- TRACK(trips0$x, trips0$y, trips0$date, trips0$id, segment = "planar")
tc <- track_cells(tr, c(50, 35))
head(tc)
#>   .seg .cell        p0         p1         dt
#> 1    0   584 0.0000000 0.16552947 1559.61865
#> 2    0   534 0.1655295 0.80332683 6009.32674
#> 3    0   535 0.8033268 1.00000000 1853.05461
#> 4    1   535 0.0000000 0.93836817 9389.31193
#> 5    1   534 0.9383682 1.00000000  616.68807
#> 6    2   534 0.0000000 0.02080966   82.46867
ts <- track_time_spent(tr, c(50, 35))
v <- numeric(50 * 35)
v[ts$.cell + 1] <- ts$time
m <- matrix(v, 35, 50, byrow = TRUE)  ## first row is the top of the grid
image(t(m[nrow(m):1, ]))
